- Workflow: `.github/workflows/auto-format.yml` in developing-today/code — scheduled treefmt pass, `cancel-in-progress: false` concurrency, `AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA` success/loop guard, bot pushes directly to main.

**Scope for this repo**
- Census tier for this repo (per developing-today/code#2017 census, tiers accepted by Drew under developing-today/code#2230, decisions ledger fleet-tiers-2230, answered 2026-11-14): Umbrella-only — census recommendation accepted under #2230; this repo is the fleet umbrella itself. - Adapt, don't blind-copy: use this repo's own formatters / treefmt (or equivalent) config; keep the PoC's invariants — (1) formatting never gates a merge, (2) a pass is never cancelled mid-commit, (3) a success marker / equivalent guard prevents re-processing and loops, (4) bot commits go directly to the default branch with a clear `style(treefmt): auto-format on main` (or repo-equivalent) message.

event: diagnosis — build leg failure isolated to the :full registry cache export (GHCR blob scope denial)
by: agent archer (kind muse, Muse sandbox seat, Lane EI — arrived here reconciling the green code/opencode legs, #37/#36)
at: 2026-11-22

The `build` job of the gated fleet-build variant is failing deterministically, at the same step, in every recent run (verified in runs 45072661780 and 45099045788):

- Failing step: `Build :full (load locally, do not push yet)`, at its final `#18 exporting cache to registry`:
  `error writing layer blob: denied: permission_denied: The token provided does not match expected scopes.`
- The `:base` build in the SAME job, with the SAME login (docker/login-action, username `dezren39`, PAT from the GHCR org secret) and the SAME cache package (`ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build`, tag `buildcache-base`), completes its `#15 exporting cache to registry` with DONE. So this is not a blanket loss of packages permission for the token.
- The difference is the `:full` cache ref (`buildcache-full`, mode=max): its layer set includes layers the base cache does not — most plausibly layers that already exist in GHCR under the `developing-today`-owned `fleet-build` package, where buildx attempts a cross-repository blob mount and GHCR denies it because the dezren39 token has no access to that package ("token does not match expected scopes" is GHCR's mount-denial wording).

Candidate fixes for the owning slice (not attempted here — this lane's items were the two green legs):
1. Drop `mode=max` on the `:full` cache-to (mode=min exports only the final stage's own layers), if the denied blobs are inherited/base-stage layers.
2. Grant the token access to the developing-today `fleet-build` package (package access settings / link the package to a repo the token can write), if the mount source is that package.
3. Switch the `:full` cache-to to `type=gha` and keep registry cache for `:base` only.

Until one lands, every gated variant run goes red on this job even though all six warm-export legs pass — the workflow-level failure signal currently means "cache export denied", not "a leg is broken".

dezren39/fleet#32.title: Optional warm-export legs fail silently inside green runs
dezren39/fleet#32.body: Run 41600076443 completed SUCCESS while its warm-export (nix) leg failed in 8 seconds: the manifest names shell 'fleet' for nix, but the fleet repo's nix submodule pointer (6d02290f) predates dezren39/nix#1383, which added devShells.fleet — so the export errored with 'flake does not provide attribute devShells.x86_64-linux.fleet' and the manifest's 'optional' flag swallowed it. build-full and smoke passed; nothing for nix was realised or pushed. This is the third distinct false-green mode for this leg (after the cache-key skip, dezren39/fleet#30).\n\nFix the visibility, not just the instance (the pointer bump is a separate PR): an optional leg that errors should be impossible to miss in a green run — e.g. export.sh emits a workflow warning annotation and a step-summary table of per-leg outcomes (realised / cache-hit / FAILED-optional), and the smoke job lists which repos' closures the published image actually carries.

comments.body: Second instance, run 41603446506 (nix leg): the shell realised and pushed to Cachix fine, but the R2 nix-cache push failed — DNS could not resolve nix-cache.developing-today-llc-domains-0.workers.dev after 5 retries — and export.sh logged only 'WARNING nix nix-cache push failed (non-fatal)'. The leg and run stayed green; without reading the leg log there is no way to know one of the two cache sinks missed the closure. The per-leg outcome table proposed in this issue should cover push results per sink (realised / R2 ok|failed / Cachix ok|failed), not just realisation.

Variant shakedown evidence (run [41628624575](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41628624575), 2026-11-03 ~11:36–11:39 UTC): with the gated variant's strict mode on, **all five legs failed at the R2 nix-cache push** — `Could not resolve host: nix-cache.developing-today-llc-domains-0.workers.dev` inside the job containers, on every nix retry, across all five runners in the same window. The hostname resolves normally from outside, and the plain pipeline pushed 4 of 5 closures to R2 earlier the same day (run 41603446506), so this reads as a transient workers.dev DNS failure window on the runner network rather than a config error. The strict gate did its job (nothing published on failed sinks; the five standing leg issues #35–#39 collected the failure comments). Mitigation landing with the variant: bounded retries around the hosted-cache pushes in export.sh strict mode (3 attempts, 20s/40s backoff) to ride out short windows; longer outages still fail the leg and are retried by the 30-minute cadence.

Diagnosis update (2026-11-03 ~12:47 UTC): this is NOT a transient resolver window and NOT Azure-specific. Public resolvers (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and Google 8.8.8.8, checked via DoH) both return **NXDOMAIN** for `nix-cache.developing-today-llc-domains-0.workers.dev` — the name no longer exists in public DNS. A probe workflow (fleet PR #42, since removed) confirmed the name fails to resolve from both a GitHub host runner and inside the fleet-build container, while the workers.dev parent zone resolves fine. The plain pipeline pushed to this name successfully earlier the same day (~08:00 UTC), so the Worker's workers.dev name disappeared during the morning of 2026-11-03 — consistent with the Worker being deleted/renamed or its workers.dev route disabled in the Cloudflare account. The R2 bucket's contents are unaffected; every substituter pointing at the workers.dev URL is dead until the name is restored (consumers fall back to cache.nixos.org + Cachix). The variant's strict gate is behaving correctly throughout: it refuses to publish while a sink is down.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-11-03, via the laptop's wrangler OAuth against the CF API): **the Cloudflare account's Workers subdomain was renamed** from `developing-today-llc-domains-0` to `developing-today`. The nix-cache Worker was never deleted or modified (untouched since 2026-10-07, subdomain enabled) and is live and verified at **https://nix-cache.developing-today.workers.dev** (proper nix-cache-info). The R2 bucket nix-cache-nars is intact. Every hostname under the old subdomain died with the rename. The audit log isn't readable with the available credentials, so who/when renamed it is unattributed; fleet evidence brackets it to the morning of 2026-11-03 (~08:00 UTC pushes still worked).

Fix in flight: migrate every fleet reference from the dead hostname to `nix-cache.developing-today.workers.dev` — fleet Containerfile/export.sh, the repos' nixConfig substituters (code, opencode, openchamber, dezren39/nix), and the fleet Actions secret NIX_CACHE_UPLOAD_URL (already updated). The signing key and all cached content are name-independent and unchanged.

Closing — the R2 cache outage is resolved and the variant it unblocked has now passed its full gate end-to-end.

## Root cause

Every push to the R2-backed nix cache failed DNS on `nix-cache.developing-today-llc-domains-0.workers.dev` (NXDOMAIN). The Cloudflare account's Workers subdomain had been **renamed** from `developing-today-llc-domains-0` to `developing-today`. The `nix-cache` Worker and the R2 bucket (`nix-cache-nars`) were never touched — only the hostname moved.

## Fix

Pure hostname migration to **`https://nix-cache.developing-today.workers.dev`** (the signing key and cached content are name-independent): the fleet Actions secret `NIX_CACHE_UPLOAD_URL` was updated, and the old host was swapped out in fleet (PR #44), opencode (PR #1523), and openchamber (PR #1458).

## Proof

Variant run [41666346758](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41666346758) (head 735210686, completed 2026-11-03T15:51:07Z) is the first full gated pass: conclusion **success** — check, all five warm-export legs (pushing to the R2 cache at the new host), the build job with its smoke step, commit-pins, and the report job all green.

Follow-on cleanup: the fleet-build mirror workflow in developing-today/code is being retired separately (developing-today/code PR #5028), since the variant now publishes the org image directly.

dezren39/fleet#30.title: fleet-build: nar cache key ignores the manifest shell — shell changes silently keep warming the old shell
dezren39/fleet#30.body:
Found 2026-11-03 while verifying the dezren39/nix fleet-shell fix (fleet#29 + dezren39/nix#1383): the publish run 41598906446 went green with warm-export (nix) in 49s — because the export step was SKIPPED on a nar-cache hit. The cache key is fleet-nar-<repo>-<flake.lock hash> only: it does not include which shell the manifest names. dezren39/nix's lock never changed, so the entry saved when the manifest said 'default' satisfied the run after the manifest switched to 'fleet' — the published :full still contains the default shell's closure, and the fleet shell has never actually been realised by the pipeline.

Same hazard for every repo: any future manifest shell change (or a repo adding/renaming its fleet shell) is silently ignored until the lock happens to change or a fresh_build is dispatched.

Fix: include the manifest's shell token for the repo in the nar cache key (fleet-nar-<repo>-<shell>-<lock hash>). First run after the fix re-exports everything once under honest keys — which is also the first true end-to-end test of nix's fleet shell.

dezren39/fleet#70.title: fleet-build smoke: offline shell step dies on code@main flake.lock drift + root-owned checkout
dezren39/fleet#70.body:
Surfaced by the #28 verification run [41834923394](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41834923394) (2026-11-04). The gating did its job — every job executed — but smoke's `Warmed shell opens OFFLINE` step failed inside its test subject:

- Smoke checks out developing-today/code @ main (44b2dd56) and runs `nix develop .#fleet --offline` as vscode in the published :full container.
- During evaluation, nix tried to UPDATE code's flake.lock: input `openchamber/opencode` resolved from `github:developing-today-forks/opencode/4175c630` (2026-11-03, as locked) to `github:developing-today/opencode/ce1aec22` (2026-11-04) — code's flake inputs drifted during today's fork reorganization, so the committed lock no longer matches the flake's resolution.
- Writing the updated lock then failed: `error: opening file ".../code-check/flake.lock": Permission denied` — the checkout is root-owned and nix runs as vscode (the safe.directory fix earlier in the step covers git reads, not lock writes).

Two candidate fixes (either or both):
1. Make the smoke checkout writable by vscode (chown the code-check tree, like other steps do), so a lock refresh cannot die on permissions — though an `--offline` smoke arguably should not be refreshing locks at all.
2. Pin smoke to the same code rev the warm-export leg realised (the committed submodule pin / cache key basis) instead of floating on code's current main, so the smoke tests exactly what was warmed.

Pre-existing environment/subject drift, not a pipeline gating defect: the last fully green runs were 2026-11-03, before code's inputs moved. Filed from the #28 verification pass per fleet practice.

comments.body:
Fixed and proven.

**Fix (both candidates from the issue, combined):**
- PR #75 (merge a0ed31f5): the smoke no longer checks out developing-today/code at floating main. It checks out this repo, resolves the committed `code` submodule pin live (`git ls-tree HEAD code`), and checks code out at exactly that rev — the rev the warm-export legs realised, whose lock is the nar-cache key basis, so the smoke tests the closure that was actually warmed. The `nix develop` also runs against a vscode-owned copy (`code-smoke`) of the checkout, so a lock refresh, should one ever be attempted, lands in the copy instead of dying on the root-owned tree.

Run 41564555311 (fresh_build dispatch, 2026-11-03): the optional warm-export (nix) job died abruptly mid-step at 2h02m (step 8 stuck in_progress, logs never uploaded — BlobNotFound; runner/container killed, consistent with resource exhaustion on dezren39/nix's oversized default shell). Because build-full has needs: warm-export (the whole matrix), the job failure skipped build-full and smoke, failing the publish — even though all three REQUIRED repos (code, opencode, openchamber) exported fine and their caches were complete.

The graceful path works (an optional export STEP failure is continue-on-error, so the job succeeds); only a hard job death exposes this. The real required-repo guard already exists inside build-full: the merge step hard-fails if a required repo's nar cache is missing or empty.

Proposed fix: give build-full (and smoke, transitively) an if: ${{ !cancelled() }} so a failed optional matrix leg cannot block the publish, relying on the merge step's required-repo checks as the gate. The 60-minute warm-export timeout added in PR #27 already halves the bleed on a repeat (122 min -> 60), but the publish should not depend on optional legs at all.

## Problem

`sync-upstream.yml` cannot run on the ~100 new org fleet forks created 2026-11-06 (org saturation program, developing-today/code#6645), for two stacked reasons found by live proof (dezren39-dev/fleet run 42328445423, job "pull upstream main", 401 "A JSON web token could not be decoded"):

1. **Key/app mismatch.** The workflow hardcodes `app-id: 5454422` (the *developing.today* app) and reads `secrets.FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. The org-level `FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` now set on all admin orgs holds the **fleet app's (5612056)** key (BWS `github-app.developing-today-fleet.private-key`) — a JWT for app 5454422 signed with 5612056's key is rejected. BWS holds **no** private key for app 5454422 (only the backup app 5562183 and fleet app 5612056 keys); the working repo-level secret on developing-today/fleet + dezren39/fleet was set 2026-11-04 from a source not in BWS.
2. **App not installed.** Even with the right key, the sync mints a token for app 5454422, which is installed only on developing-today / -forks / -vendored / -fork. On the other ~99 orgs neither 5454422 nor 5612056 is installed, so app-token sync cannot authenticate there at all. (Installs are browser/sudo-gated; tracked on code#6645.)

## Options

- **A. Re-point sync to the fleet app (5612056)** — change `app-id` to 5612056 so it matches the org-level key already everywhere; still needs the fleet app installed per org (same browser trip as Blacksmith/CodeRabbit).
- **B. Re-point sync to the GHCR_ORG_PAT** (classic PAT, repo+workflow scope — the `workflow` scope exists precisely to allow pushing workflow files). Works on every org today with zero installs; loses the app-identity/ruleset-bypass properties the current design comments describe.
- **C. Vault the 5454422 key in BWS** and install app 5454422 on all orgs — most faithful to the current design, most browser work.

Until one lands, new org forks are current only as of their fork time (all contain the post-PR#86 fleet-run; forks created before the #86 merge carry the pre-#86 file and also cannot sync). Proof that the forks otherwise run fleet jobs: dezren39-dev/fleet runs 42328489467 + 42330094546, sleep-atomic/fleet run 42328728480 (all success, GitHub leg).

Context: org saturation run 2026-11-06 (code#6645 comment has the full matrix).

developing-today/code#13774.title: fleet actions exec: live short-lived exec sessions inside Actions runners, coordinator-handed-off
developing-today/code#13774.body:
# fleet actions exec: live short-lived exec sessions inside Actions runners, coordinator-handed-off

Drew's order, 2026-11-23 15:17 CST: implement an alternate `fleet actions exec` mode that may become the primary — agents connect into GitHub Actions runners and exec commands themselves, temporary and short-lived like the commander/route subcommand family (#13717). The central coordinator (#13765) establishes the connection handoff; the fleet command background-watches the run after handoff.

## Premise (verified first-hand, 2026-11-23)

- **Coordinator (#13765)** has a complete design of record: broker verbs `/placement-claim|confirm|release|claim-status|load`, a coordinator sweep in the queue broker, client integration with a **singular fallback** that names itself via `placement_path`. Its build is routed separately; this mode composes with the design (claim a slot for the session's host surface when the verbs answer; proceed singular and record `placement_path` when they don't) and never forks it.
- **Fleet action constellation:** the generic fleet action lives in **dezren39/fleet** — composite action `.github/actions/fleet-command`, dispatch workflows `fleet-command.yml` (repo-queue dispatch runner) and `fleet-run.yml` (generic runner; developing-today/fleet fork adds runner choice + cache deltas that must survive syncs). Fixes land on dezren39/fleet main and sync to the forks.
- **Existing IO pattern (dispatch path):** command output lives in the Actions run log; reusable output chains via the `fleet-output` artifact (`previous_run_id` input downloads the prior run's artifact); caches via actions/cache and the R2 nix cache (`cache.push_nix` → signed `nix copy` to the R2 cache URL, skipping quietly when secrets are absent).
- **PM push surface exists:** `crates/fleet-queue/src/needs_drew.rs` (#8568) emits needs-drew alerts into the PM aggregator throat — `POST http://127.0.0.1:4870/api/alerts`, Bearer token resolved **by name** through fleet-secrets, body `{source, key, severity, title, body, needsDrew:{ledgerId, question, context, options[], links[]}}`, deduped by (source, key). The notification presents choices; this is the emergency-extension push path.
- **Rendezvous constraint (#10356):** the sandbox has no inbound path; every route names its rendezvous. Runners are on the public internet and the queue broker lives on the laptop — so this mode needs a public door in the commander/mcpx pattern (Worker gate + tunnel → laptop), path-scoped to the session verbs.
- **Route family shape (#13717):** timeout required by construction; the serving form is named in output.

## Method survey — direct runner access, filtered by the public-log leak

The hard filter: **most off-the-shelf runner-access methods print SSH/connection info into the run log, and in a public repo the log is world-readable.** Any method whose connection material can appear in logs is disqualified, however convenient.

| Method | Shape | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tmate (mxschmitt/action-tmate et al.) | Runner opens tmate session; SSH string + web URL printed to log | **Rejected** — connection string in public logs is the exact leak |
| upterm (action-upterm) | SSH via upterm server; connection info printed to log; actor-limiting exists | **Rejected** — same leak; allowlists don't unpublish the log |
| tailscale/github-action | Runner joins the tailnet; reach it by tailnet name, nothing secret prints | Viable but not picked: couples runner access to tailnet enrolment/ACLs for every caller, and #13752 thread 1 is actively designing *away* from Tailscale-only reach |
| cloudflared + Access on the runner | Runner dials out to Cloudflare; requester authenticates via Access | Viable; the estate already runs this door pattern (commander/mcpx). Kept as the door technology, not the session protocol |
| iroh endpoint on the runner | NodeId is a public key — printing it leaks nothing; auth is the keypair (#13752 thread 2) | Right long-term transport for the fleet binary; not the v1 session protocol (pilot is scoped to seat→amd, and this mode needs the coordinator handoff semantics first). The session protocol below is transport-shaped so iroh can carry it later |
| **Runner-side agent dials OUT to the coordinator (chosen)** | The workflow starts a small agent (a mode of the fleet binary). The agent proves it is inside the run with the job's **GitHub OIDC token** (fetched from the Actions runtime, never logged), registers with the broker, and holds an outbound long-poll. Commands flow requester → broker → agent; IO flows back the same way | **Chosen** — no inbound path, nothing connection-shaped ever exists outside the two endpoints, the session handle is a public identifier (safe in logs), and the handoff *is* the coordinator's job in #13765's design |

Runner-side auth detail: the broker verifies the OIDC JWT against GitHub's JWKS and checks `repository`, `workflow`, `job_workflow_ref`, `run_id`, `run_attempt` claims against the session row the coordinator created at dispatch. Requester-side auth is the existing broker seat auth. Workflow inputs carry only the handle + non-secret parameters — never a token (inputs are visible on the run page; secrets would be masked but dispatch cannot receive them).

## Design

**Three pieces, one flow.**
1. **Action** — dezren39/fleet `.github/actions/fleet-exec-session` (composite, fleet-command conventions): sets up the pinned fleet binary, runs `fleet actions agent` for the session, ships the egress helper on PATH.
2. **Workflow** — dezren39/fleet `.github/workflows/fleet-exec.yml` (workflow_dispatch; inputs: handle, target repo/ref optional checkout, runner, lease/max seconds, hide-logs flag; `permissions: id-token: write`; job timeout = max lifespan + grace).
3. **Subcommand** — new `actions` domain in pkgs/fleet (fleet-registry + verbs.md in the same change): `fleet actions exec` group in the #13717 family shape — `--timeout` required by construction, serving form named in output.

**Flow:** requester runs `fleet actions exec start` → subcommand asks the coordinator to claim a slot for the host surface and create the session row (singular fallback per #13765 when the coordinator doesn't answer) → subcommand dispatches `fleet-exec.yml` with the handle → coordinator/subcommand binds run id + attempt (the **handoff**: handle, `OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID`, attempt) → runner agent registers via OIDC → requester execs via `fleet actions exec run <handle> -- cmd`, attaches/streams, renews, closes.

**Broker verbs** (new module `crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue/actions_exec.rs`, routed in `turso_queue::dispatch` beside the placement coordinator's; house conditional-UPDATE atomicity; DDL beside `placement_sessions`):
- `/actions-exec-open` (seat) — create session {handle, host_repo, seat, lease_until, max_until, hide_logs, state}.
- `/actions-exec-bind` (seat/coordinator) — record run_id + attempt.
- `/actions-exec-register` (agent, OIDC-verified) — bind agent to session, state `live`.
- `/actions-exec-poll` (agent) — long-poll for commands + lease state.
- `/actions-exec-command` (seat) — enqueue one command {cmd_id, text, timeout_s}.
- `/actions-exec-io` (agent) — append IO chunk {cmd_id, seq, stream, data}; `/actions-exec-result` (agent) — exit code, cmd terminal.
- `/actions-exec-stream` (seat) — IO chunks after a seq (attach + background watch read this).
- `/actions-exec-renew` (seat) — extend lease within max; past max → `extension-required`.
- `/actions-exec-extend-request` (seat) — past-max extension: creates the request **and emits the needs-drew alert** (source `fleet-actions-exec`, key `actions-exec-ext:<handle>`, options approve/deny, links to the run + this issue). Session enters `extension-pending` with a short decision grace so a live agent isn't killed mid-question.
- `/actions-exec-extend-decide` (seat acting on Drew's answer) — applies or denies. **Known gap:** the phone tap → broker write-back is the PM stack's next phase; v1's write-back is a seat running this verb on Drew's recorded answer. The alert is the push; the verb is the closest existing surface.
- `/actions-exec-close` (either side) — terminal; agent exits, workflow step ends.

**Disconnect tolerance:** requester disconnect is a non-event (broker holds commands, IO, lease). Agent network blips retry with backoff against the long-poll. Reconnect = re-attach with the same handle; the session and any running command survive a short grace window, mirroring the laptop attach pattern.

**Lease discipline:** lease = `--timeout` at start (required, no default). Hard cap = `--max-lifespan` (default 30 min, ceiling 120 min — the fleet-run leg cap). The agent enforces the lease locally as well as via the broker (dies at expiry even if partitioned, after a final IO/egress flush). Renewals move `lease_until` up to `max_until`; past that, only an approved emergency extension (push above) moves it, each approval bounded (+30 min).

**File egress:** the Action puts `fleet-exec-put <file>` on the session PATH: it copies the file into the session outbox (uploaded as the `fleet-exec-out` workflow artifact when the session step ends) **and** PUTs it to R2 (S3-compatible; credentials arrive as workflow secrets, are masked by GitHub, and are never echoed; absent credentials skip the R2 leg quietly, the fleet-run cache pattern).

**Log visibility + IO decision:** by default the agent echoes session IO to its own stdout, so commands and output land in the Actions run log (the dispatch path's existing visibility). `--hide-logs` on the subcommand turns the echo off. **Decision:** the transport is brokered in both modes (it is the handoff mechanism, not a visibility feature); the broker's IO chunk store is the cache of record either way — with logs visible it is the low-latency attach/watch source, with logs hidden it is the *only* IO path back to the requester. No second IO system is built.

**Background watch:** after handoff the subcommand can follow the run without holding the requester's terminal: `fleet actions exec watch <handle>` streams broker IO + run status (polled via the placement GitHub client) until terminal; `start --detach` returns after handoff and records the handle in the local session store so `watch`/`attach`/`run` resolve it from any seat (the portable `OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID` form works too).

## Slices

1. This issue: premise + survey + design.
2. Action + workflow in dezren39/fleet (agent bootstrap in proof mode: build the agent from a code ref in the runner; production pins the released fleet binary).
3. Broker verbs + DDL + tests (rusqlite fake-pipeline pattern from #13765's proof bar).
4. Runner agent (`fleet actions agent`): OIDC register, poll/exec/stream loop, lease enforcement, egress helper.
5. Subcommand (`fleet actions exec` group): start/run/attach/watch/renew/extend/close + coordinator composition + singular fallback naming.
6. PM push wiring for emergency extension (needs-drew throat emission + decide verb).
7. Live proof (below), runbook note in `doc/agents/remote-build-and-test.md`, verbs.md, PRs, merge on green.

## Proof bar

One live end-to-end run, recorded here: subcommand → coordinator handoff (handle + run id + attempt named) → exec a command on the runner → `fleet-exec-put` a file out to **both** the workflow artifact and R2 → requester disconnect/reconnect resumes the same session → renewal extends within the cap → a short-lease session dies at its cap unrenewed. Plus the leak acceptance test: **read the produced public workflow logs end to end and show no connection material** (no tokens, no OIDC material, no credential values — handles and run ids only).

Lane ACTIONS-EXEC. If the platform execution-risk check stops a build step, the stop is recorded here with the exact slice state for routing to a laptop session.

## Design amendment — tiered lease-extension policy (lane ACTIONS-EXEC-3)

Drew's policy, in his words (2026-11-23 ~17:06 CST), recorded before implementation; the implementation below follows this record exactly:

- "Up to a certain extension, or the first extension, can be approved automatically with just a notification."
- "Then maybe one that, if I don't respond, another push notification will approve, but I have time to deny."
- "After that, I would have to manually approve, or if it's over a certain size or something."
- "Make sure the push notification has enough detail, and I can click into it to see the run, where it's coming from, what the session name is, and other important details."

### The tiers (defaults are named tunables in `turso_queue::actions_exec`)

| Tunable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `EXT_AUTO_SIZE_CAP_S` | 1800 (30 min) | Largest single ask the auto tiers may grant — equal to the existing per-approval bound `MAX_EXTENSION_S`. A request whose **raw** ask exceeds it is tier 3 even when it is the session's first extension. |
| `EXT_TIER1_MAX_COUNT` | 1 | Extension #1 of a session is tier 1. |
| `EXT_TIER2_MAX_COUNT` | 2 | Extension #2 is tier 2 (subject to the caps); #3 and beyond are tier 3. |
| `EXT_AUTO_TOTAL_CAP_S` | 3600 (60 min) | Cumulative approved extension seconds the auto tiers may grant over a session's life; a request that would push the total past this is tier 3. (With the current size/count caps the count cap binds first; the total cap is an independent guard so a future retune of one cap cannot silently widen the auto surface.) |
| `EXT_DENY_WINDOW_S` | 600 (10 min) | Tier 2's deny window: silence at window end approves. |
| `EXTENSION_GRACE_S` | 300 (unchanged) | Tier 3's decision grace past the lease, as in v1. |

Evaluation happens in `/actions-exec-extend-request`, from the session's `(ext_count, ext_total_s, raw ask)`:

- **Tier 1 — AUTO + NOTIFY.** The extension is applied inside the request itself (the same conditional-UPDATE approval shape `/actions-exec-extend-decide` uses today); `ext_state = 'auto-approved'`. One notification-only push: a plain PM alert with **no** needsDrew choice block (the #9177 plain-alert shape).
- **Tier 2 — NOTIFY + DENY WINDOW.** The request pends with `ext_decide_after = now + EXT_DENY_WINDOW_S`. While it pends, the session's hard deadline covers the window — `max(lease, decide_after) + EXTENSION_GRACE_S` — so the agent is not killed mid-window; the agent enforces the broker-reported deadline from its poll, as today. A deny via `/actions-exec-extend-decide` ends the extension at once (the session ends at its current cap); an approve via the same verb applies it immediately; **silence approves at window end**, settled lazily by the next verb that touches the session (the agent polls continuously, so in practice the poll settles it) with `ext_state = 'silence-approved'`. Exactly one push per request — the deny-window warning is the push; no second "it approved" push.
- **Tier 3 — MANUAL ONLY.** The v1 flow, unchanged in shape: pending + needs-drew approve/deny push + `/actions-exec-extend-decide` applies or denies (`ext_state = 'approved'` / `'denied'`).

`ext_count` / `ext_total_s` increment on **every** approval (auto, silence, manual) and never on a deny, so the tier ladder measures what was actually granted.

### Push payload (every tier, per Drew's detail requirement)

Session handle (`fx-…`) and the session's `context` link when one was recorded at open (new optional open field below); requesting seat; host repo; workflow + run id + run attempt with a click-through run URL (attempt deep link); the agent's stated reason (already accepted by the verb, now also stored on the row as `ext_reason`); lease state — opened-at, granted lifespan, `lease_until`, `max_until`; the ask (+N min); cumulative extensions before → after (count + minutes); the tier; and the tier's consequence of deny / timeout. Tier 2's needsDrew options are **[deny, approve now]** (deny first — it is the choice that changes the default); tier 3's stay **[approve, deny]**.

Alert keys gain the extension ordinal — `actions-exec-ext:<handle>:<n>` — so successive extensions on one session no longer dedupe-suppress each other's pushes at the throat; the one-live-request-per-session rule is still enforced by the pending guard, not by the key.

### Schema (additive, house migration pattern in `turso_queue::core`)

New `actions_exec_sessions` columns, added to the DDL of record and landed on existing databases by `pragma_table_info`-checked `ALTER TABLE`: `ext_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `ext_total_s INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `ext_tier INTEGER`, `ext_decide_after TEXT`, `ext_reason TEXT`, `context TEXT`. The open verb accepts an optional `context` string (a seat-supplied task/issue link for the session, threaded from a new `fleet actions exec start --context` flag); when absent, extension pushes link this issue as the session's home, as v1 did.

### Named gap (unchanged from v1, stated plainly)

The phone tap → broker write-back is still the PM stack's next phase: tier-2 denies and tier-3 answers land via a seat-run `/actions-exec-extend-decide` on Drew's recorded answer, not via a direct phone→broker channel. For tier 2 that means a deny must be relayed before the window closes; the 10-minute window is sized with that relay in mind. The push **deep link itself** (run URL in `needsDrew.links` / the plain alert body) is wired by this lane — the aggregator already carries links; what does not exist yet is the tap-to-broker answer path.

### Proof

Unit tests (rusqlite fake-pipeline pattern, named oracles): tier 1 auto-approve moves max/lease and counts; tier 2 approves on silence after the window; tier 2 deny inside the window ends it at the cap; tier 3 stays manual (no settle past grace); oversized raw ask escalates a first extension to tier 3; cumulative cap escalates to tier 3; alert bodies carry the full payload per tier with ordinal keys. The v1 test `extension_request_and_decision_move_the_max` is reworked onto tier-3 requests (an oversized ask), since a plain first request is tier 1 now.

**ACTIONS-EXEC-3 — build started.** Implementing the tiered lease-extension policy recorded in the design amendment directly above (comment 7116645799). Worktree `~/wt-actions-exec-3` on the laptop, branch `lane/actions-exec-3-tiers`, off origin/main `094f977b923`. Scope: broker verbs/coordinator decision path + needs-drew payload + fleet client/CLI outcome printing + tests. The halted in-vivo proof (agent-install step) is explicitly **not** this lane's scope. Primary checkout dirt named and left untouched: `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`, `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py`, `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py`.

AUDIT-7 Lane 5 (DESIGN-REVIEW, #13876) — verdict: **sound; correctly subordinated to #13765**.

- Dependency handling is exemplary: the design composes with the coordinator's verbs when they answer and proceeds singular (recording `placement_path`) when they don't — it never forks #13765's design, so its head is not blocked by the coordinator build.
- The method survey's hard filter (connection material in public run logs disqualifies tmate/upterm) is the right first gate and is applied before convenience.
- Like #13765, the design of record lives only on this issue — no doc/ record. Same suggestion: land a dated doc/ record.
- Minor: the emergency-extension path reuses the #8568 needs-drew push; the design should state what happens when a session outlives its runner's job limit mid-exec (the handoff watcher's timeout behaviour) — one paragraph would close it.

**Tier defaults (as recorded in the amendment):** `EXT_AUTO_SIZE_CAP_S` 1800 · `EXT_TIER1_MAX_COUNT` 1 · `EXT_TIER2_MAX_COUNT` 2 · `EXT_AUTO_TOTAL_CAP_S` 3600 · `EXT_DENY_WINDOW_S` 600.

**Tests:** fleet-queue suite 616 passed / 0 failed (incl. the new tier oracles: tier-1 auto-approve, tier-2 silence-approves, tier-2 deny, tier-3 manual gate, size-cap escalation, cumulative-cap escalation, deny-window hard-deadline cover, and the three per-tier alert-body tests); fleet bin + fleet-registry + docs-inventory 141 passed / 0 failed. Local clippy could not run: the laptop's clippy/rustc pair is version-split (1.99.1/1.99.0) and the matched rustup toolchain binaries do not execute in this shell context — main-branch CI is the backstop.

**Live verification (production broker, gen 8):** session `fx-e64e5bdf0b5a97668450` opened broker-side with `context` = this issue's URL (stored and echoed by stream). Extension 1 (600s): **tier 1, outcome `auto-approved`**, counters 1 / 600s. Extension 2 (600s): **tier 2, outcome `pending-deny-window`** with `decide_after` 10 minutes out; a decide with `approve` absent (deny) landed inside the window — `ext_state` denied, counters unchanged. Session closed. The tier-2 silence path and tier 3 are unit-proven (the silence path needs a real 10-minute window; not waited out live).

**Push payload — one live gap, precisely:** both raises were attempted by the broker and the alert bodies are unit-tested per tier (full detail set + run deep link + ordinal keys), and the same raise path succeeded earlier today (17:08 CST, gen 7). Tonight the PM alerts throat (127.0.0.1:4870) returned **HTTP 401** for both raises: the current BWS value of `pm-aggregator.alerts-intake-token` disagrees with the token the long-running aggregator process (up since 2026-11-22 20:26 CST) expects — confirmed by a direct probe with the by-name-resolved token, also 401. This is a PM-stack/token-side mismatch, not a payload defect; it drops ALL broker-raised pushes (needs-drew included) until fixed. Filed as #13902 (PM alerts throat rejects the current intake token) with the evidence and fix shapes. The standing write-back gap from v1 is unchanged: until the PM stack's answer-write-back phase lands, tier-2 denies / tier-3 answers are executed by a seat running `/actions-exec-extend-decide` (request shape `{handle, approve: bool}`) on Drew's recorded answer.

developing-today/code#13189.body:
**Problem.** The fleet-command dispatch container cannot run JavaScript-repo verification commands: it has no `bun` on PATH. A dispatched run for an openchamber branch failed in ~8 s with `bash: line 1: bun: command not found` (exit 127) before any test executed.

Evidence: dispatch run https://github.com/developing-today-forks/fleet/actions/runs/45154877923 (repo developing-today-forks/openchamber, ref lane-qg-2501, command began `bun install --frozen-lockfile && cd packages/web && bunx vitest run ...`), 2026-11-23.

**Why it matters.** Dispatch-first is the standing route for build/test verification of lane work. The Bun-based repos (openchamber, opencode, and the code repo's own JS packages) cannot be verified through it at all today; lanes fall back to laptop-local runs. Sibling of #13159 / #13168 (the same container's `nix develop` defects): the container's toolchain does not cover the repos it is dispatched against.

**Suggested shape.** Bake bun into the dispatch container image alongside the existing toolchain, or document a supported bootstrap step in the fleet-command runbook (`pkgs/fleet/doc/agents/remote-build-and-test.md`) so dispatched commands can rely on it. Acceptance: a dispatched `bunx vitest run` against an openchamber branch executes the suite (pass or fail on the tests, not on a missing binary).

**Fix:** [dezren39/fleet PR #109](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/pull/109), merged as `c4e83d2cae35468f41ad3c55f0d5331cc1b44d43`.
